title: How a baseball can stop a healthy heart ⚾
subject: heart
description:
Is there an AED at your field? 👇

Commotio cordis is sudden cardiac arrest from a blow to the chest, with no damage to the heart itself. The hit has to land during about 1% of the heartbeat. The US Commotio Cordis Registry logged 216 cases by 2012, and survival depended on how fast a defibrillator arrived. In that registry, 37% of athletes hit were wearing chest protectors. This video is not medical advice.

Sources: Tainter & Hughes, "Commotio Cordis", StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf, NIH); Maron et al. 2013, "Increasing survival rate from commotio cordis", Heart Rhythm 10(2):219-223 (US Commotio Cordis Registry, Minneapolis)

scenes.text: One baseball to your chest can stop your heart.
No broken ribs. The hit just has to land in about 1% of a heartbeat.
That's the rising edge of the T wave. A blow then throws the heart into ventricular fibrillation.
The registry in Minneapolis logged 216 cases by 2012, mostly boys around 15.
In a 2013 Heart Rhythm study, 40% survived with a shock or CPR inside 3 minutes. Later, only 2 of 42 did.
